# Results — Study 170 (Alphabetical-Bias) on real S&P 500 tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Monthly equal-weight
returns and volume for S&P 500 names grouped by first letter (A–C = "early alphabet"
vs D–Z = "late alphabet"), tested against a full-universe equal-weight baseline.
As-of **2026-06-15**; prices from Yahoo Finance (daily, resampled to monthly last-close).
Survivorship bias: universe is the **current** S&P 500 (point-in-time constituents
not available here — this is named on the Signal axis).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Universe | S&P 500 current constituents (via `quantlab.universe.sp500_symbols`) |
| Tickers loaded | 503 total: **128 early (A–C)**, 375 late (D–Z) |
| Tickers with cached daily data | 502 |
| Date range | 2000-02-29 → 2026-06-30 |
| Months | **317** |
| Early-alphabet obs | 35,888 |
| Late-alphabet obs | 103,785 |
| Panel fingerprint | `7ac909f898e2` |

## Volume channel — the attention effect (H1)

Monthly log-volume comparison (A–C vs D–Z equal-weight groups), Newey-West HAC
t-stat on the monthly log-volume difference.

| Group | Mean daily volume (shares) | n months |
|---|--:|--:|
| **A–C (early alphabet)** | **2,570,083** | 317 |
| D–Z (late alphabet) | 2,345,835 | 317 |

- **Volume ratio (early / late): 1.096** — early-alphabet stocks trade ~9.6% more
  daily volume on average.
- **HAC t-stat: +10.34** — highly significant; the attention effect is robust over
  25 years of data.

**H1 confirmed.** Jacobs & Hillert (2015) are correct: alphabetical list position
affects retail attention and trading volume. The effect is economically small
(~10%) but statistically unambiguous.

## Return channel — does attention earn a premium? (H2)

Monthly equal-weight return spread (A–C minus D–Z), Newey-West HAC t-stat.

| Metric | Value |
|---|--:|
| **Mean spread** | **−6.90 bps/month** |
| HAC t-stat | **−1.24** |
| Annualised Sharpe of spread | −0.256 |
| n months | 317 |

- The return spread of **−6.90 bps/month** has HAC t = **−1.24**: statistically
  **indistinguishable from zero**.
- The point estimate is slightly *negative* — early-alphabet stocks marginally
  *underperform* late-alphabet stocks in this sample, the opposite of what the
  "attention premium" would predict.
- **H2 rejected.** Additional retail attention does not translate into a return
  premium in the S&P 500 universe over this period.

## Per-letter Bonferroni scan

Testing each of the 26 letters vs the cross-section mean, plus the main A–C
group test = **27 hypotheses total**. Bonferroni-corrected threshold:
|t| ≥ 2.897 (p < 0.00185).

| Rank | Letter | Mean (bps/mo) | HAC t-stat | Bonferroni sig? |
|---|---|--:|--:|:--:|
| 1 | B | −22.3 | −2.29 | No |
| 2 | K | −26.4 | −2.06 | No |
| 3 | Z | −44.3 | −1.60 | No |
| 4 | N | +18.5 | +1.41 | No |
| 5 | D | +14.1 | +1.24 | No |

**0 out of 26 letters survive the Bonferroni correction.** The single most
significant letter (B, t = −2.29) would only pass an *uncorrected* 5% threshold,
and even then it is *negative* — consistent with noise, not a predictable premium.
Multiple comparisons kill any letter-level finding.

## Positive control — engine validates on synthetic data

On a deterministic synthetic panel with a planted 30 bps/month early-alphabet
return bias (300 stocks × 240 months), the engine detects the bias (t > 2).
On a null panel (no bias planted), it correctly finds nothing. The engine is
a faithful detector of return differences; the real tape simply has no return
wedge to find.

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** Volume channel robust (t = +10.34); return channel
  indistinguishable from zero (t = −1.24). Survivorship bias in universe
  (current-constituent-only) is named. 0 letters survive Bonferroni.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No return edge; low-turnover alphabet portfolio
  adds no gross alpha vs an equal-weight S&P 500; concentration risk vs benchmark.
- **Attention effect — REAL BUT NOT TRADABLE.** ~10% volume premium for A–C
  names is unambiguous over 25 years. Markets price it without leaving a return wedge.
